title: Stock Label Run
user: Small shops and makers who receive stock and need a local, repeatable way to turn a purchase list into correct barcode labels and a print receipt.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A local-first barcode tool creator reports that small businesses and sellers face expensive subscriptions or awkward tools when printing bulk inventory labels.
A Grocy user requests that stock-entry label-print webhooks include product details and the stock-entry object during purchase, showing the handoff from receiving to labeling is incomplete.

recurrence: Current 2025–2026 evidence points to the same receiving-time workflow: label creation must retain item and stock-entry context without an enterprise label suite.
current_workaround: Copy product names into label templates, create barcodes one at a time, or pay for BarTender-class software.
incumbents_and_gap: BarTender, ZebraDesigner, Sortly, and inventory suites are capable but costly or broad; small receiving runs need a local CSV-to-label workflow with a proof of what printed.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that imports a CSV, validates SKU/barcode values, lays out label sheets, prints browser/PDF labels, and saves a printable run receipt. Non-goals: barcode allocation authority, POS, inventory database, or printer-driver management.
success_measure: A pilot user prints a 50-item receiving run with zero manual retyping and reconciles every printed label to an imported SKU in under 15 minutes.
monetization: one-time — label generation is a local utility and print volumes should not create a monthly tax.
constraints: Support only documented barcode symbologies and checksum validation; preserve CSV locally; do not claim marketplace-specific label compliance without test fixtures.
why_distinct: The differentiator is receiving-run traceability, not another online barcode generator.
